candidate.answerReason: After a red first draw, five blue balls remain among nine balls. Therefore the required ordered probability is \((5/10)(5/9)=5/18\).

methods.label: Condition on the first draw
methods.explanation: The probability of red on the first draw is \(5/10\). Given that the first ball is red, 9 balls remain, including all 5 blue balls, so the conditional probability of blue on the second draw is \(5/9\). Multiplying gives \((5/10)(5/9)=5/18\).
methods.levelReason: This uses the changing ball count and the elementary multiplication rule within the stated elective scope.

methods.label: Count ordered pairs of balls
methods.explanation: Label the 10 balls so that they are distinct. Since the random draw treats ball labels symmetrically, all ordered pairs of distinct balls are equally likely. There are \(10\cdot9=90\) possible pairs: 10 choices for the first ball and 9 remaining choices for the second. A red ball followed by a blue ball gives \(5\cdot5=25\) favorable pairs. Each possible draw determines exactly one ordered pair, so no outcome is omitted or counted twice. Hence the probability is \(25/90=5/18\).
methods.levelReason: Counting equally likely ordered pairs uses elementary multiplication of choices, at no higher prerequisite level than conditional multiplication.
